record.field:
Retrieve records from any Odoo model with filtering capabilities. Wraps Odoo's search_read.
## Parameters
- `model` (str, required): Odoo model technical name (e.g. "res.partner", "sale.order"). - `domain` (list, default []): Odoo domain filter. Each condition is a 3-element list `[field, operator, value]`. Conditions are AND-ed by default; use `"|"` (OR) or `"!"` (NOT) prefix operators to combine. - `fields` (list[str], default all): Field names to return. Specify a small subset to save tokens. - `limit` (int, default 100): Max records to return. Use small values when exploring.
## Domain Operators
Comparison: `"="`, `"!="`, `">"`, `">="`, `"<"`, `"<="` Set membership: `"in"`, `"not in"` (with a list value) Text match: `"like"`, `"not like"`, `"ilike"` (case-insensitive, **the usual choice for text**), `"not ilike"`, `"=ilike"` (full match, supports `%` and `_` wildcards) Existence: `"=?"` (treats False as match-any) Many2one path: use dotted field: `["partner_id.country_id.code", "=", "US"]` Polymorphic / Many2many "child of" hierarchy: `"child_of"`, `"parent_of"`
## Domain Logical Operators (Polish notation, prefix the AND/OR they group)
- `"&"` AND of next 2 conditions (implicit between adjacent conditions) - `"|"` OR of next 2 conditions - `"!"` NOT of next 1 condition
Examples: - `["|", ["state", "=", "draft"], ["state", "=", "sent"]]` — state is draft OR sent - `["&", "|", ["a","=",1], ["b","=",2], ["c","=",3]]` — (a=1 OR b=2) AND c=3 - `["!", ["active", "=", True]]` — active is not True
## Common Query Patterns
1) Get all active partners with name like 'pharma': `{"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["active","=",True], ["name","ilike","pharma"]], "fields": ["id","name","email"], "limit": 50}`
2) Recent sale orders this year: `{"model": "sale.order", "domain": [["date_order",">=","2026-01-01"], ["state","in",["sale","done"]]], "fields": ["id","name","amount_total","partner_id"], "limit": 20}`
3) Find by Many2one related field name (dotted path): `{"model": "res.users", "domain": [["partner_id.country_id.code","=","CN"]], "fields": ["id","name","login"]}`
4) Filter Many2many via 'in' (matches if ANY id is associated): `{"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["category_id","in",[1,2,3]]], "fields": ["id","name","category_id"]}`
5) Empty / not-set field (works for any optional field): `{"model": "sale.order", "domain": [["partner_invoice_id","=",False]], "limit": 10}`
6) Boolean OR across two text fields: `{"model": "res.partner", "domain": ["|", ["name","ilike","acme"], ["company_name","ilike","acme"]], "fields": ["id","name","company_name"]}`
7) Date range (Char date-string comparison works for date/datetime fields): `{"model": "mail.message", "domain": [["date",">=","2026-05-01"], ["date","<","2026-06-01"]], "fields": ["id","subject","date"], "limit": 100}`
8) Count-like check (limit=1 to test existence): `{"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["email","=","x@y.com"]], "fields": ["id"], "limit": 1}` — empty list ⇒ no match.
9) Selection field exact match: `{"model": "sale.order", "domain": [["state","=","sale"]], "fields": ["id","name"]}` (use the Selection KEY, not the label)
10) Find records updated after a timestamp: `{"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["write_date",">","2026-05-20 00:00:00"]], "fields": ["id","name","write_date"]}`
## Tips
- Always specify `fields` for known queries — saves tokens and response size. - For text search, `"ilike"` is almost always what you want (case-insensitive contains). - For Many2one fields, the value returned is `[id, display_name]`; pass the integer `id` (or use a dotted path on the related model). - For Selection fields, use the technical key (e.g. `"sale"`), not the label (e.g. `"Sales Order"`). - For Many2many / One2many fields, the value returned is a list of ids. - Dates: pass `"YYYY-MM-DD"` for Date fields, `"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"` for Datetime fields. - If you're unsure of a model's field names or selection values, use `odoo_model_inspector` first. - Limit high (e.g. 1000) only when you actually need all rows — large results consume tokens fast.

Create one or multiple new records in any Odoo model. This tool allows you to insert data into the database by specifying the model name and either: - A dictionary of field values using the "fields" parameter for a single record, OR - A list of dictionaries using the "records" parameter for multiple records at once. - Either 'fields' or 'records' must be provided
Examples: 1. Single record: {"model": "res.partner", "fields": {"name": "John Doe", "email": "john@example.com"}} 2. Multiple records: {"model": "res.partner", "records": [{"name": "John Doe", "email": "john@example.com"}, {"name": "Jane Smith", "email": "jane@example.com"}]}
REQUIREMENT — schema first: If you do not already know the target model's schema (which fields are required / readonly, which are Selection with what keys, which are Many2one to what target model), you MUST call `odoo_model_inspector` first to fetch it. Do not guess field names, do not invent Selection keys, do not pass a name where an id is expected. A failed create wastes a tool call AND an LLM round-trip — one cheap inspector call upfront prevents both.
Due to its data modification capabilities, this tool requires user consent before execution.

Update existing records in any Odoo model. Targets records by **id only**, applies the `values` dict. Defaults to **limit=1** for safety — set explicitly when you want to update multiple rows. Requires user consent.
REQUIREMENT — schema first: If you do not already know the target model's schema (which fields are writable / readonly, which are Selection with what keys, which are Many2one to what target model, Many2many command syntax), you MUST call `odoo_model_inspector` first to fetch it. Do not guess field names, do not invent Selection keys, do not pass a name where an id is expected. A failed update wastes a tool call AND an LLM round-trip — one cheap inspector call upfront prevents both. The `values` parameter is required and non-empty; omitting it is a schema mistake that the inspector would have caught.
## Parameters
- `model` (str, required): Odoo model technical name (e.g. "res.partner", "sale.order"). - `domain` (list, required): **Must filter by `id` only.** Either single-id or id-list — no other operators or fields are allowed here. If you don't know the id yet, use `odoo_record_retriever` first to find it. - `values` (dict, required): Field-name → new-value pairs to write. - `limit` (int, default 1): Safety cap on how many records can be updated.
## Domain — id filter only
Allowed forms (only these two):
- Single record: `[["id", "=", 42]]` - Multiple records: `[["id", "in", [42, 91, 184]]]` (and set `limit` ≥ list length)
NOT allowed in this tool (use retriever first to look up the id, then pass id here): - Filtering by name / state / email / any other field - Dotted paths (`partner_id.country_id.code`) - OR/NOT operators - `ilike` / `like` text search
This restriction prevents wrong-record bulk updates.
## Values dict
For most field types, just `field: value`: ```json {"name": "Updated", "active": false, "amount_total": 1234.5, "date_order": "2026-05-21"} ```
For Many2one, pass the integer id (not a record dict, not a name): ```json {"partner_id": 42, "user_id": 7} ``` To clear: `{"partner_id": false}`.
For Selection fields, pass the technical KEY (not the label): ```json {"state": "sale", "priority": "1"} ```
## Many2many command syntax
Many2many updates use **command tuples** wrapped in a list. Each command is `[code, id, values]`.
| Code | Form | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `3` | `[3, id, 0]` | Unlink (remove association, keep the linked record) | | `4` | `[4, id, 0]` | Link (add to set; idempotent) | | `5` | `[5, 0, 0]` | Clear all associations (no delete of linked records) | | `6` | `[6, 0, [id1, id2, ...]]` | Replace the set with this exact list |
### Many2many examples
Add tag id=5 to partner id=42 (preserves other tags): ```json {"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["id","=",42]], "values": {"category_id": [[4, 5, 0]]}} ```
Replace partner's tags with exactly [1, 2, 3] (drops all others): ```json {"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["id","=",42]], "values": {"category_id": [[6, 0, [1, 2, 3]]]}} ```
Remove tag id=5 from partner id=42 (does not delete the tag record itself): ```json {"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["id","=",42]], "values": {"category_id": [[3, 5, 0]]}} ```
Clear all tags: ```json {"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["id","=",42]], "values": {"category_id": [[5, 0, 0]]}} ```
Combine: add tag 5 AND remove tag 9 in one call: ```json {"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["id","=",42]], "values": {"category_id": [[4, 5, 0], [3, 9, 0]]}} ```
## One2many — do NOT operate from this side
Don't try to add / update / delete One2many children via the parent. Operate **on the child model directly** instead: - To create a child: call `odoo_record_creator` on the child model with the parent's id in the inverse field. - To update a child: call `odoo_record_updater` on the child model with the child's id. - To delete a child: call `odoo_record_unlinker` on the child model with the child's id.
Example: instead of "add an order line to sale.order id=10", create directly on `sale.order.line`: ```json {"model": "sale.order.line", "fields": {"order_id": 10, "product_id": 1, "product_uom_qty": 2}} ``` (via `odoo_record_creator`)
## Common Update Patterns
1) Mark a record inactive: `{"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["id","=",42]], "values": {"active": false}}`
2) Bulk-update fields on a known set of ids (explicit `limit`): `{"model": "sale.order", "domain": [["id","in",[10,11,12]]], "values": {"user_id": 7}, "limit": 3}`
3) Change Many2one + Selection in one call: `{"model": "opportunity.opportunity", "domain": [["id","=",91]], "values": {"therapeutic_area": 3, "decision": "go"}}`
4) Clear an optional Many2one: `{"model": "res.partner", "domain": [["id","=",42]], "values": {"parent_id": false}}`
5) Date update: `{"model": "sale.order", "domain": [["id","=",10]], "values": {"date_order": "2026-05-21 09:30:00"}}`
## Tips & Safety
- **Look up ids with `odoo_record_retriever` first**, then pass them here. This tool only accepts id-based domains by design. - Default `limit=1` protects against runaway updates. When using `["id","in",[...]]`, set `limit` to match the list length. - For Selection fields, use the technical KEY (e.g. `"sale"`), not the label (e.g. `"Sales Order"`). - For Many2one, pass an int id (or `false` to clear). Don't pass a name or display string. - For Many2many, `[[4, id, 0]]` is **add-only** — much safer than `[[6, 0, [...]]]` which replaces the whole set. - For One2many children, operate on the child model directly (see "One2many" section above). - If unsure about field type / required flags / selection keys, use `odoo_model_inspector` first.

Delete existing records from any Odoo model. This tool allows you to remove data from the database by specifying the model name and domain filters to identify records to delete. For safety, it defaults to deleting only one record at a time. Due to its data modification capabilities, this tool requires user consent before execution.

**VERY HIGH RISK TOOL:** Executes a specified method on an Odoo model or specific records. Provide the model's technical name, the method name, and optionally a list of record IDs, positional arguments ('args'), and keyword arguments ('kwargs'). If record_ids is null/empty, the method is called on the model itself (e.g., for `search`, `create`, `@api.model`, `@staticmethod`). **WARNING:** This tool can modify or delete data, trigger complex actions, or cause system errors if used improperly. It bypasses standard UI workflows. **IMPORTANT:** The LLM using this tool MUST explicitly ask the user for confirmation before EVERY execution, clearly stating the model, method, records (if any), and arguments being used. Private methods (starting with '_') are disallowed by default unless 'allow_private' is explicitly set to true (use with extreme caution). Returns a JSON representation of the method's result or an error message.

Comprehensive inspection of an Odoo model providing a complete analysis of its structure. This tool retrieves detailed information about:
1. **Basic Model Data**: Name, description, module, and inheritance structure. 2. **Fields Analysis**: Types, properties, relations, required/readonly status, and help text. 3. **Methods Inspection**: Signatures, docstrings, decorators (@api.model, @api.depends, etc.), and method types.
Use this tool to understand any Odoo model's structure, fields, and available methods. You can filter fields and methods by name or type, limit the number returned, and include/exclude private elements (those starting with '_').
This information is essential for: - Understanding available data structures - Determining which fields to use for record creation/updates - Finding appropriate methods to execute with the model_method_executor tool - Building domain filters for record retrieval
Perfect for exploring unfamiliar models before performing operations on them.
NOTE — finding the model name: If you don't already know the exact technical model name (e.g. "res.partner", "sale.order.line"), look it up in the `ir.model` registry first via `odoo_record_retriever`. Search by `name` (human-readable label) or by `model` (technical name) with `ilike`: {"model": "ir.model", "domain": [["name", "ilike", "partner"]], "fields": ["model", "name"], "limit": 20} {"model": "ir.model", "domain": [["model", "ilike", "sale.order"]], "fields": ["model", "name"], "limit": 20} Pick the right technical `model` value from the results, then pass it to `odoo_model_inspector`.
